To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel method for detection of relatively more stable modes in the records of climate variables that have strong red-noise background, which is based on evaluating and statistically testing regularity of the modes against the red-noise null hypothesis, and we have successfully applied it in detection of the period 7.7–8 years oscillatory mode in the monthly N.A.O. index and temperature records from several European locations.

the regularity index computed from a coarse grained estimation of mutual-information enhances the test sensitivity in detection of relatively regular modes, and that period 7.7–7.8 years modes are detected in the monthly N AO index and temperature records from several European locations.

1) The enhanced MC SSAs can detect period 7.9 years oscillations in records of monthly temperature from several European stations, as well as period 7.7 years oscillations in monthly NAO indices, 2) The period 7.5-8.0 years oscillatory modes are found in the monthly temperature records from several European stations and the NAO index, 3) These oscillatory modes are detected in records of monthly mean temperature from 12 locations

the detection of oscillatory modes embedded in red noise and with the evaluation of their regularity.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 7.8 year period is not an artifact of the analysis, but is a real oscillation embedded in the monthly temperature and NAO index time series.
the enhanced MC SSAs are very efficient tools for detection of relatively more deterministic modes embedded in the red noise background.
the enhanced MC SSAs are a powerful method for detection of oscillatory modes, which are not necessarily periodic, in time series of climate variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the enhanced MC SSAs are a useful tool for analysis and detection of oscillations with periods ranging from several years to decades, in the presence of red noise.

the enhanced MC SSAs are very useful for the detection of oscillations in time series with colored noise, and that the detected period 7.9 years oscillatory modes are likely related to solar activity.
, the enhanced MC SSA is able to identify the period 7.7 years oscillatory modes, in addition to other oscillatory modes of periods 2.3, 3.8, and 6.5 years, in the temperature and NAO index records.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the enhanced MC SSAs are useful for detection of irregular oscillatory modes in climate records, and that these modes are not necessarily associated with periodic oscillations, as they are usually defined in the context of climate dynamics.
the regularity index is a useful and reliable complement to variance-based test in the MC SSA.
the MC SSA can be used as a tool to detect and analyze oscillatory dynamics embedded in red noise.
